sentences.text: Inland rules use the same blasts for a different purpose.
When power-driven vessels are in sight of one another and meeting or crossing at a distance within half a mile of each other, each vessel shall indicate her intended maneuver.
One short blast means I intend to leave you on my port side.
Two short blasts means I intend to leave you on my starboard side.
Three short blasts means I am operating astern propulsion.
Upon hearing the one or two blast signal, the other vessel shall, if in agreement, sound the same whistle signal and take the steps needed to pass.
If she doubts the safety of the proposal, she sounds the danger signal.
Inland light signals may be white or yellow, and are synchronized with the whistle.
